newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria sends two more ships to Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sends two more ships to Sierra Leone.

text.p: Nigeria has despatched two more naval ships to Sierra Leone in a move suggesting West Africa's major power remains committed to forcing coup leaders there to restore democracy.
The frigate Aradu and the fast attack boat Ekpe have left to join two other Nigerian naval ships already in waters off Sierra Leone.
"I can confirm that NNS Aradu left for Sierra Leone on Sunday and NNS Ekpe left on Monday," said a military spokesman.
He declined to comment on local newspaper reports that the reinforcement of the Nigerian-led West African ECOMOG force meant an attack was imminent.
"That is for the ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) to say," he added. Nigeria's own military ruler General Sani Abacha is the current chairman of the regional grouping.
Aradu, the flagship of the Nigerian navy, is a German-built frigate which can attack air, surface and shore targets. Ekpe was also built in Germany.
The coup by junior officers in Sierra Leone on May 25 toppled the elected president, Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, and Nigeria is in the forefront of a campaign to restore him to power.

The shelling of Sierra Leone's capital Freetown by Nigerian gunboats in a show of force last week failed make an impact on the coup makers who responded by naming their own ruling council and saying they would not reinstate Kabbah.
The coup makers are backed by rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), who took up arms against the Sierra Leone army in 1991 and have flooded into Freetown since the coup.
Witnesses said heavy mortar fire and shooting rang out briefly across Freetown late on Tuesday, causing panic in the city where many fear a Nigerian attack to restore Kabbah.
A spokesman for the coupmakers said the outburst, which lasted 10 minutes, followed a quarrel between Sierra Leonean and Nigerian soldiers at Lungi airport.
